idiom_name: hand-written zip/apply over Result; Combine's Publishers.Zip for streams
implementation_notes: Swift's stdlib Result provides map, flatMap and mapError only - all fail-fast - so combining independent results requires a hand-written zip or apply that pairs the successes and keeps the first failure. What replaces the classic structure for asynchronous streams is the Combine framework's Publishers.Zip (pairwise, order-preserving) and combineLatest (most recent), neither of which accumulates errors, so full error accumulation still needs an error-collecting Failure type. The classic form is justified when several independent parses must be reported together; for control flow, chaining with try/? is simpler.
pitfalls: A hand-written zip keeps only the first failure, so 'report every error' needs a Failure type that itself collects messages - otherwise the applicative shape is only cosmetic.
Combine's Zip and CombineLatest complete when any upstream completes and drop unmatched values, so a stream combine can silently lose the last element.
Result is only Equatable/Codable when its parameters are, which complicates assertions and transport; mapError at the boundary rather than deep inside the combining code.
Adding an arity means adding another zip overload; variadic forms via parameter packs (Swift 5.9+) avoid the explosion but complicate the call sites.
